description.invocation: One complete offline batch=32 inference: infer(model, pixels) (resnet_inference.py:15-16), i.e. model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode() on the pretrained FP32 ResNet-18, with pixels the pre-built GPU-resident contiguous 32x3x224x224 float32 NCHW batch (images[torch.arange(32, device='cuda') % 3], resnet_inference.py:29). Completion boundary is the torch.cuda.synchronize() after the forward, matching the source timing at resnet_inference.py:42-47. Excludes model loading, host-to-device input transfer, reference construction, correctness checks, warmup/repeat statistics, result saving and optional --profile diagnostics.
notes: Command provenance (intent.json): python resnet_inference.py --assets /root/autodl-tmp/dev/v6-work/validation-assets/resnet18 --output /tmp/original-resnet; no --warmup/--repeats/--profile flags, so common.py defaults apply.

Work vs harness: adapter.run() repeats exactly one infer() call on the fixed GPU batch. The reference/actual pair construction, close_check/negative_check, assert of exact top-1, warmup loop, 5-repeat timing loop with reset_peak_memory_stats, summarize/save of result.json and profile_once (common.py:87-105) are benchmark/quality infrastructure.

Objective metric key is the source sample field latency_ms (resnet_inference.py:48), median over 5 clean samples per summarize(); the same per-call metric the project already records for every workload row. The user's goal selects latency for the offline row; it must not be renamed to a cached-only or throughput metric.

The row's other goals (images_per_second max; peak_allocated_bytes min with constraint images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio 0.95) belong to other objectives and are not imported as latency constraints; the source attaches no constraint to latency goals. peak_allocated_bytes is still recorded per sample by the harness.

Batch semantics preserved: batch=32 formed by cycling the 3 preprocessed fixture images (dog1, dog2, astronaut; arange(32) % 3); FP32 NCHW, GPU-resident, .contiguous(); pixel transfer to device happens once before timing.

Numerical policy preserved (common.py:34-42): torch.float32, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark=False, float32_matmul_precision('highest'), 4 CPU threads / 1 interop, manual_seed 20261020, torch.inference_mode for all measured calls.

Quality semantics: full 1000-class logits compared with torch.testing.assert_close(atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4); discrete top-1 labels compared exactly via torch.equal(actual.argmax(-1), reference.argmax(-1)) (require_exact_top1) - these argmax label outputs need exact comparison, no tolerance; negative control must reject a +1 corruption of the reference (common.py:79-84); reference tensors saved as offline-reference.pt (pixels + logits).

Single-GPU, single-process workload: .cuda() plus torch.cuda.set_device(0); no process group, no NCCL; run_suite.py exposes exactly one GPU via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES for this case. No communication collector fields requested; latency is ordinary end-to-end per-call time, not a diagnostic kernel time.
Assets stay at their absolute paths and are pinned by asset-manifest.json (microsoft/resnet-18 revision 65a5785d9156231087c481e0c7dd33a5ff6f7e3e); pixels.npy verified as (3, 3, 224, 224) float32.

assumptions: The user's 'offline batch=32' maps to the source workload row id "offline" (batch 32) in workloads.json; 'reduce latency' selects the per-call latency_ms metric the harness already records for that row, not the row's throughput or memory goals.
warmup=2 and repeats=5 apply (common.py:24-25 defaults) because the intent command passes neither flag.

The throughput-floor constraint images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio=0.95 is attached to the memory goal of this row and is intentionally not applied to the latency objective; the source defines no constraint for latency goals.
Output artifacts (offline-reference.pt, result.json) are written by the harness under --output; the timed unit itself only produces logits.
